page.title: makeurquiz — Free Online Quizzes & Best Online Learning Platform

findings.title: Page scrolls sideways on a phone (450px wide at 390px)
findings.evidence: e.g. div.flex.items-center ends at 450px; a.inline-flex.items-center “Get started” ends at 450px.
findings.fix: Find the fixed-width element (tables, code blocks, images, grids with min-width) and give it max-width: 100% or overflow-x: auto. Test at 390px.

findings.title: Row items are off by a few pixels
findings.evidence: span#lovable-badge-text “Edit with” and span#lovable-badge-logo sit in the same row but their top edges differ by 2px (870 vs 868). 1px is sub-pixel noise; 2–3px is a mistake, not a decision.
findings.fix: Align them on the same axis: use align-items on the parent, or give both the same margin-top. If the offset is intentional, make it ≥ 8px so it reads as deliberate.

findings.title: One h2 is a different size from the other 5
findings.evidence: “Common questions” is 36px; the other h2s are 48px (36px ×1, 48px ×5). Same semantic level should get the same treatment.
findings.fix: Pick one size for h2 and set it once in CSS. If one of these is really a sub-heading, change its tag instead of its size.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: AI purple / purple-to-blue gradient accent
findings.evidence: 29 elements use a violet/indigo accent (hue 260–310°), 29 as a gradient, e.g. div.w-9.h-9. This is the single most-cited vibe-coded tell in the Reddit corpus (#2 overall).
findings.fix: Pick one base hue that means something for this product and derive the palette from it. If you keep purple, make it a decision: one accent, solid, used sparingly.

findings.title: Gradient-filled text (9)
findings.evidence: span.bg-clip-text.text-transparent “free online quizzes” uses background-clip: text with a gradient. Decorative, hurts contrast, and reads as generated.
findings.fix: Use a solid colour. Emphasis comes from size and weight, not a rainbow.

findings.title: Rounded icon tile above 9 headings
findings.evidence: 9 near-square 44px boxes with a background sit directly above headings. The icon-in-a-tinted-square above every feature title is the default generated feature grid.
findings.fix: Remove the tile backgrounds and let the icon sit inline with the heading, or drop the icons and let the headings carry the row.

findings.title: Head is missing: title is 68 chars (cuts off ~60)
findings.evidence: Has JSON-LD. One h1, good.
findings.fix: Ten minutes of <head> work: title under 60 chars, canonical URL, lang attribute, favicon, and an Organization or WebSite JSON-LD block.

findings.title: Nested cards (×4)
findings.evidence: “Card inside card (div)” · “Card inside card (div)” · “Card inside card (div)”
findings.fix: Cards inside cards create visual noise and excessive depth. Flatten the hierarchy — use spacing, typography, and dividers instead of nesting containers.

findings.title: A lone badge “New · AI-powered” that does nothing
findings.evidence: A 181×24px pill that is not clickable, is not one of a set of tags, and labels something the surrounding text already makes clear. Badges imply a category system; a single one is decoration.
findings.fix: Delete it. If the information matters, fold it into the sentence next to it. Reserve pills for things that are actually one of several (filters, statuses, tags you can click).
findings.citation: no-slop ‘status pill with dot’ heuristic (MIT); Fountain Institute tell #7 (status dots)

findings.title: 24 rounded panels on one page
findings.evidence: Rounded corners on every container is one of the ranked vibe-coded tells (#5 in the Reddit corpus).
findings.fix: Round the things that are interactive or elevated; let sections and layout containers stay square.

findings.title: 1 row of three identical cards
findings.evidence: Three 389px-wide cards of equal weight (“rounded-lg border text-card-foreground shadow-sm border-border/60 bg-card”, “rounded-lg border text-card-foreground shadow-sm border-border/60 bg-card”, “rounded-lg border text-card-foreground shadow-sm border-border/60 bg-card”). The hero + three feature cards skeleton is tell #9; equal weight tells the reader nothing is more important than anything else.
findings.fix: Decide which one matters and make it bigger, or turn the three into one sentence each under a single heading. Break the symmetry once.
findings.citation: vibecoded-design-tells #9; 21st.dev: uniform features is a top-5 tell

findings.title: Eyebrow chip above the hero headline
findings.evidence: “Trusted by 12,000+ educators & teams worldwide” (12px, pill) sits directly above a 72px h1. The tiny label + giant headline pairing is the default generated SaaS hero.
findings.fix: Fold the label into the headline or the first sentence. If it's an announcement, make it a real link somewhere else.

findings.title: 15 untouched shadcn/ui cards
findings.evidence: Class strings like “rounded-lg border bg-card text-card-foreground shadow-sm group” are the component library's defaults, unmodified. Fine as scaffolding; as the final look it's tell #1.
findings.fix: Change the tokens (radius, border colour, shadow) once in your theme so the components stop looking like the docs page.

findings.title: Frosted-glass panels (6)
findings.evidence: 6 elements combine backdrop-filter blur with a translucent background, e.g. header.sticky.top-0. On 17% of Show HN launches.
findings.fix: Use a solid surface. Translucency only earns its place when something meaningful is behind it.

findings.title: Centered hero: big headline, centered sub, centered buttons
findings.evidence: h1 at 72px, centered, with 4 centered blocks under it. On 23.5% of Show HN launches. It's the layout every builder emits when nobody chooses one.
findings.fix: Not a problem on its own, but combined with other tells it's the skeleton. Left-align and put the product next to the headline, or lead with the product itself.

findings.title: 5 tracked all-caps section labels
findings.evidence: Small uppercase, letter-spaced labels like “New · AI-powered” above sections. On 10.5% of Show HN launches, and usually redundant with the heading under them.
findings.fix: Delete the label or fold its word into the heading.

findings.title: Blurred colour blobs behind the content (3)
findings.evidence: div.absolute.-top-16 is a blur(64px) wash. The aurora backdrop is the default "atmosphere" of generated heroes.
findings.fix: Remove it and let the content carry the first screen. If you want atmosphere, use one real image.

findings.title: 9 em dashes in 3.3k characters
findings.evidence: 2.7 per 1,000 characters. Humans use them; generated copy uses them in nearly every paragraph, and readers have learned to notice.
findings.fix: Keep the ones that do work; turn the rest into commas, periods, or parentheses.
findings.citation: Impeccable em-dash-overuse; Slopdar em-dash signal; HN thread

findings.title: Formulaic closer
findings.evidence: “Join thousands of”
findings.fix: Open with the specific thing the product does; close with the specific next step. Both are places where a template sentence is doing the job of a real one.

findings.title: h3 is used at 3 sizes, consistently
findings.evidence: Sizes: 16px ×5, 18px ×6, 20px ×6. “Teachers & schools” is 20px, “Is makeurquiz really free?” is 16px. Each size is used more than once, so this is a system rather than drift; but it means the same tag is doing two jobs.
findings.fix: If the 16px ones are sub-sections, make them h4. Screen readers and search engines only see the tag.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: Stat banner: 12K+ · 2.4M · 98%
findings.evidence: A row of 3 big numbers with small labels. On 12% of Show HN launches. Real numbers are fine; the pattern reads as template when the numbers are round, unsourced, or "99.9% uptime" on a weekend project.
findings.fix: Keep it only if each number is real, specific and checkable (link the source). Otherwise fold the one true number into a sentence.
